chapter: A musical family and the old New Orleans bands
title: Marvin Kimball, the showman banjoist with Papa Celestin
summary: Kimball twirled his Paramount banjo and played it behind his head with Celestin's band.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: And right away you begin to learn who carries weight, and who can play and who can't play and who is copying. Well, right away, when I looked around, I saw Kimball.
Marvin Kimball, a sensational banjo player.

Yeah. He was a sensation around 19... He was with Papa Celestin. He and Guy Kelly. The first [foist] time I heard [hoid] this band, I was shocked into insensibility when I heard those two. He was playing that banjo. He played "The World Is Waiting For The Sunrise." And he had this Paramount banjo. And he was a showman, and he played this banjo, he twirled it up and down, he played it behind his head. And the people were just looking at him in amazement. He came back... He must have learned that up when he went on the road before, and then he came back.

And there was Guy Kelly playing identically like Armstrong, and almost looking like Armstrong.
